## ✨ Highlights

- 🛰️ **An IPv6 anycast address is never the source of the node's own connections**: a `/128` - the address nodes announce with BGP - is now deprecated from the start. The node answers on it as before, but its own IPv6 connections leave from its other addresses: with the anycast address as their source, their replies came back to whichever node the router chose, or nowhere before the address was announced ([network configuration](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/network-configuration.md)).

## 🌐 Network

- **A `/128` is deprecated from the start** ([#345](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/345)): Linux picks the most specific, newest preferred address as the source of an outgoing connection - an anycast `/128` beside the interface's `/64` took every one, Let's Encrypt's or a backend's over IPv6 included. Added with a preferred lifetime of 0 and valid forever, it still receives and answers - HAProxy's replies leave from it -, and no outgoing connection starts from it. An IPv4 `/32` needed nothing: Linux picks the address on the gateway's subnet. Found before announcing an IPv6 anycast address on a production cluster.

## 📖 Docs

- [Network configuration](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/network-configuration.md), [BGP](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/bgp.md): a `/128`'s source behaviour.
- [v2026.10.26-2's lab campaign](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.26-2.md) ([#344](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/344)): a network change on the VRRP master, and the same IPv6 anycast address on both nodes behind RouterOS 7.25 (BGP over IPv6, BFD, multipath), before and after.

## 🧪 Tests

- netmgr's network-namespace test: a `/128` comes up deprecated, and the node's own IPv6 and IPv4 connections never leave from the anycast addresses.
- `qemu-vrrp-ipv6-test`: node A's own connections to node C, over IPv6 and IPv4, leave from its LAN addresses with the anycast `/128` and `/32` in place.
